scores.visual_critic_note: Deliberate Tol palette and clear typographic hierarchy elevate this above generic, but Singapore's near-zero seasonal variance collapses its violins into flat horizontal dashes, breaking the shape encoding for an entire row.
scores.encoding_integrity_note: Structurally honest: y-scale is data-driven via d3.extent, violinScale uses scaleLinear correctly for density-to-width (not area/bubble), KDE bandwidth uses Silverman's rule with a reasonable 0.5°C floor, and shared maxDensity ensures cross-cell comparability; no truncated baselines, no dual axes, no radius deception.
scores.stress_test_note: No brush/zoom or cross-view dispatch; pointer events abstract mouse/touch correctly; medians and scales are pre-computed outside handlers, eliminating stale-closure risk; no D3 transitions means no mid-flight interrupt concern; only mildly expensive work (array sort + quantile on 35 values) runs on pointerenter, not pointermove.
scores.cognitive_load_note: 72-cell grid (6 cities × 12 months) stays readable because the two-color split-violin encoding is consistent across every cell, the shared y-scale lets eyes scan rows and columns without re-orienting, and hover interaction dims non-relevant rows — the only real strain is that 88px cell height compresses fine distributional shape, and Singapore's near-zero seasonal amplitude produces flat needle shapes that read as outliers rather than valid distributions.
